headline: Semis jumped 5.1% in a dip-buying rally, but the month is still -17.5% and a half-point December Fed hike is now on the table with CPI due.
regime: Semis ETF +5.1% and Nasdaq +2.7% on the day, but the semis are -4.1% on five days and -17.5% on the month, and VIX is still +31% on the month at 19.97. The 10-year is 4.86% and Fed governor Waller put a half-point hike into the mix, so rates cap any rebound. Every AI segment bounced 3-11% on the day yet is down 20-30% on the month, except power (-11.5%) and hyperscalers (-8.2%). Power and hyperscalers are the only groups positive on five days, which fits a rebound of short covering, not new evidence.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: AAON posted record $707m sales, 84% revenue growth and raised its 2026 outlook (833e12a8ba51, 14844b0c7fe5)
Power is the only AI segment up on five days (+6.6%) and the best on the month (-11.5%) (digest segments)
NRG sold six gas plants for $4bn and raised its buyback to $3bn (7ae7703ab3be); X-energy got a construction permit for four reactors (0eb57beec65c)
Against: Vertiv fell 11% in a week as the Democratic sweep revived data-centre slowdown fears (c8718052ee86)
Against: AAON disclosed a first-half restatement; grid is -3.8% and cooling -7.6% on five days (833e12a8ba51, digest segments)
theses.change_note: +2: AAON's raised outlook is fresh order evidence and power led on five days, though the restatement and the Vertiv drop keep it from moving further.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: TSMC October revenue rose 59.7% to NT$367bn on Nvidia and Apple orders (60ad92e4a222, 8ed37387914c)
Onto reported revenue of $410m, up nearly 90% on the year, with a record $1.3bn backlog (2eadf9cefb52, 8aad7e8ca2aa)
Neocloud GPU rental prices are rising even as the stocks fall (e7f92c850f5c)
Against: banks that funded neoclouds are hesitating, which can slow the supply of new capacity (a29afdc0468c)
theses.change_note: +2: TSMC and Onto prints are hard demand data and GPU rental prices are rising; funding hesitancy is the offset.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Banks that raced to fund CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle are tightening lending rules (a29afdc0468c)
Jefferies and Morgan Stanley cut targets on powered-shell names; Cantor cut IREN to $47 from $99 (fdf0aec02b07, 8d5590988167, f507b8eea075)
CoreWeave is down 65% from its May high with a sentiment problem ahead of earnings (c41d345b9e46, 2f5894c17d90)
Against: GPU rental has never been more profitable, and Wells Fargo calls CoreWeave the highest-quality neocloud (e7f92c850f5c, 65c4387c8f3f)
theses.change_note: Lenders are pulling back while the operating economics stay good; the CoreWeave print is still the test.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Micron jumped in the dip-buying session and Western Digital rebounded 9.9% after a 28% five-day fall (34d4705ffe6c, e22ab4bc08d6)
Against: memory is -14.7% on five days and -31.0% on the month, still the worst segment (digest segments)
Against: ETFs were net sellers of Micron on Nov. 6 (d52b19fe980c)
theses.change_note: -2: the segment is still the weakest on five days and there is no new cycle evidence beyond a bounce.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Alphabet lost nearly $500bn of market value on investor negativity about its spending (09e06c9e4d69)
Neocloud and Oracle borrowing is meeting tighter lending (a29afdc0468c)
Against: hyperscalers are +5.1% on five days and -8.2% on the month, the sturdiest group (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -2: the group is the strongest on five days, though Alphabet's loss shows investors still punish the spending.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Waller put a half-point December hike into the mix, depending on CPI (d50ebaa3940f)
The 10-year is 4.86% and ai_software is -6.1% on five days and -23.1% on the month (digest tape and segments)
Anthropic mistakenly sent IPO terms to banks, exposing jitters over AI investment (c9221aa2e55f)
Against: the Nasdaq rose 2.7% and the semis 5.1% in one day as buyers returned (digest tape, 34d4705ffe6c)
theses.change_note: +2: a half-point hike is a worse rate path than the market priced yesterday; the one-day rally does not offset it.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Vertiv fell 11% in a week as the midterm sweep hit data-centre stocks over Texas fears (c8718052ee86)
Against: no new restriction was reported today, and power orders and permits for reactors continue (0eb57beec65c, 833e12a8ba51)
theses.change_note: Market reaction continues but no law or moratorium appeared today.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Nvidia lost $190bn as Trump confirmed a new FBI probe; shareholders filed a class action (a74052017ff6, e2712d074f1e)
Moonshot AI accessed B300 servers through Super Micro, which may breach export controls (49e0e23d454f)
Against: Trump backed Huang, the board expressed confidence in him, and the stock bounced (0439ee046a8c, 34d4705ffe6c)
theses.change_note: Fresh governance and export-control story with a Nov. 11 deadline; the outcome is binary and unknown, so confidence is moderate.

compute.note: Nvidia at 11x forward earnings but under probe; AMD +8.9% on five days shows rotation, not safety.

foundry_equipment.note: TSMC +59.7% and Onto's $1.3bn backlog are strong, but -24% on the month and 2% FCF yields.

memory_storage.note: -31.0% on the month and -14.7% on five days; a bounce is not a floor.

networking_optical.note: Fabrinet +16.3% and Aaoi -16.6% on five days; the segment is split.

servers.note: Dell -11.8% on five days; Super Micro is tied to the export story.

power_nuclear.note: Only segment up on five days; prefer cash generators like Vistra and NRG over pre-revenue reactor names.

grid_electrical.note: Hubbell +1.8% holds; policy fear, not orders, is the drag.

cooling_thermal.note: AAON's record quarter and Trane +1.8% against Modine -13.9%; quality wins.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Lenders are hesitating and most names burn cash.

hyperscalers.note: +5.1% on five days but Alphabet's $500bn loss shows capex worries.

ai_software.note: -6.1% on five days; Datadog -16.9%, no catalyst.

risks: A hot CPI would lock in a half-point December hike and push the 10-year toward 5%.
The Nvidia probe and the Nov. 11 deadline could widen into China export curbs.
CoreWeave's earnings could confirm lenders' caution and reopen the neocloud sell-off.
Data-centre moratoria in Texas or elsewhere would hit grid, cooling and power orders.
Today's rally is dip-buying after a 17.5% monthly fall and could fade.
watch: CoreWeave and Nebius earnings, plus any bank funding comments.
Cisco's earnings for AI networking demand.
The Nvidia board probe and Nov. 11 congressional deadline.
Whether power holds its five-day lead if semis keep rebounding.
